neurological_exam.special_signs: Oral thrush present on examination. Generalized lymphadenopathy palpable (cervical, axillary bilateral). Mild left facial droop. Bilateral papilledema.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive headache and confusion over 3 weeks
patient.history_present_illness: 56-year-old right-handed African American male presenting with 3-week progressive headache, difficulty concentrating, personality change (more withdrawn and flat), and mild left arm clumsiness. He was initially evaluated at an outside hospital where a CT head revealed an enhancing brain lesion, and he was transferred for neurosurgical evaluation. He was referred with a preliminary diagnosis of 'brain tumor, likely GBM.' On further history, he reports 8 kg weight loss over 4 months, intermittent fevers (not measured at home), and night sweats. He admits to a 15-year history of unprotected sex with multiple male partners. He has not seen a doctor in over 10 years and has never been tested for HIV. On physical examination, oral thrush is noted and generalized lymphadenopathy is palpable.

findings.location: Right frontal lobe, extending to corpus callosum and abutting the right lateral ventricle. Subependymal spread along the ventricular margins.

signal_characteristics.T1: Isointense to slightly hypointense to gray matter
signal_characteristics.DWI: Restricted diffusion throughout the mass (hypercellular). Diffusion restriction is DIFFUSE and HOMOGENEOUS — not rim-restricted as in GBM or abscess.
signal_characteristics.post_gadolinium: Homogeneous enhancement — NOT ring-enhancing. The mass enhances uniformly throughout without central necrosis. This is an important distinction from GBM, which typically shows ring enhancement with central necrosis.

findings.mass_effect: Moderate perilesional vasogenic edema. 6 mm leftward midline shift. Partial effacement of right frontal horn.
findings.borders: Moderately well-defined but with subependymal spread along ventricular surface

additional_observations: HOMOGENEOUS enhancement pattern (NOT ring-enhancing) — important distinction from GBM
No central necrosis (GBM typically has central necrosis)
DIFFUSE restricted diffusion (hypercellularity) — GBM typically shows rim restriction only
mri.impression: Homogeneously enhancing periventricular mass in the right frontal lobe with subependymal spread and corpus callosum involvement. The homogeneous enhancement (without central necrosis) together with diffuse, mass-wide restricted diffusion indicates a markedly hypercellular lesion; this pattern differs from the rim-enhancing, centrally necrotic appearance typical of high-grade glioma or abscess. The differential for a homogeneously enhancing, diffusely restricting periventricular/callosal mass includes a hypercellular round-cell or lymphoid neoplasm and an infiltrative infectious process; tissue diagnosis is required. 6 mm leftward midline shift with moderate vasogenic edema

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Primary CNS lymphoma (EBV-associated DLBCL) in the setting of newly diagnosed HIV/AIDS

differential.key_features: Was the initial referring diagnosis; differentiated by homogeneous (non-ring) enhancement, diffuse DWI restriction, periventricular and corpus callosum location, and HIV/immunocompromise context
Important differential in HIV/AIDS; usually multiple lesions with ring enhancement and surrounding edema; serology and empirical trial response can help, thallium SPECT (low) vs lymphoma (high)
HIV/AIDS context; typically multiple ring-enhancing lesions with surrounding edema; thallium SPECT cold (vs hot in lymphoma) and serology help differentiate

differential.diagnosis: Brain abscess (bacterial / fungal in immunocompromised host)
differential.key_features: Possible in advanced HIV; would expect central DWI restriction and clinical sepsis signs
Open ring enhancement (incomplete on side toward cortex) and minimal mass effect are typical; this lesion shows closed/homogeneous enhancement and significant mass effect
No known primary; corpus callosum involvement and subependymal spread atypical

optimal_actions.action: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right frontal periventricular lesion, define mass effect, and plan surgery
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Heterogeneously enhancing mass with ring/irregular enhancement, central necrosis, restricted diffusion at the enhancing rim, perilesional FLAIR-hyperintense edema, and mass effect consistent with high-grade glioma

optimal_actions.action: Order pre-operative laboratory workup: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), and type & screen in anticipation of surgical biopsy/resection
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline values acceptable for surgery; identify any coagulopathy, electrolyte derangement, or steroid-relevant abnormality (e.g., hyperglycemia, hyponatremia) before craniotomy

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for diagnostic and management approach to suspected CNS lymphoma in HIV/AIDS, including the standard role of HIV testing, MRI pattern recognition (homogeneous enhancement, diffuse DWI restriction), and biopsy before tumor-directed therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that empiric steroids should be deferred until biopsy is obtained where feasible (to avoid masking lymphoma histology), and that HIV testing plus stereotactic biopsy are the diagnostic standard

optimal_actions.action: Obtain urgent neurosurgical and infectious-diseases / neuro-oncology consultation; stereotactic biopsy is required for tissue diagnosis before tumor-directed therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Multidisciplinary plan including tissue acquisition, molecular profiling, and adjuvant treatment per current standards

optimal_actions.action: Obtain neuro-oncology consultation for adjuvant therapy planning and molecular-marker-guided treatment selection
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Plan for concurrent chemoradiation (Stupp protocol with temozolomide) for IDH-wildtype GBM; alternative chemoradiation regimens for other tumor types or for atypical histologies

optimal_actions.action: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess tumor vascularity and target highest-grade region for biopsy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Elevated rCBV (typically > 1.75) in enhancing component supports high-grade neoplasm and helps direct biopsy

optimal_actions.action: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize tumor metabolic profile
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Elevated Cho/NAA ratio with lipid-lactate peaks supports high-grade malignancy and helps differentiate tumor from treatment-related change at follow-up

optimal_actions.action: Order CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as staging to exclude an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is on the differential
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No extracranial primary malignancy identified, supporting primary brain tumor as the working diagnosis

useless_tools.rationale: Echocardiogram has no role in the diagnostic workup of suspected high-grade glioma absent a specific cardiac question (e.g., suspected paraneoplastic endocarditis)
Cardiac monitoring is unrelated to the diagnostic workup of a brain mass and adds resource cost without informing management

harmful_tools.rationale: Lumbar puncture is contraindicated in suspected intracranial mass with significant midline shift (6 mm): the pressure gradient created by LP risks transtentorial or tonsillar herniation. Even when LP is otherwise safe, CSF studies are low-yield for primary brain tumor diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: MRI must precede any lumbar puncture when a mass lesion is suspected, to identify mass effect and herniation risk before LP

critical_actions: Obtain urgent neurosurgical consultation for tissue diagnosis (stereotactic biopsy or maximal safe resection) and operative planning
Obtain MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol) before any invasive procedure
Administer dexamethasone (loading dose 10 mg IV, then 4 mg IV every 6 hours) to reduce vasogenic edema and mass effect (6 mm midline shift)
Obtain HIV testing and infectious workup (toxoplasma serology, CD4 count, viral load) given systemic features (weight loss, lymphadenopathy, oral thrush)
Defer empiric corticosteroids until after stereotactic biopsy if clinically feasible, to avoid masking lymphoma histology
Obtain pre-operative labs (CBC, BMP, coagulation, type & screen) before craniotomy/biopsy
Plan multimodal treatment per molecular and histological profile (e.g., Stupp protocol — concurrent chemoradiation with temozolomide for IDH-wildtype GBM)
contraindicated_actions: Do not perform lumbar puncture in the setting of mass effect (6 mm midline shift) — herniation risk
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide, alkylating chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given upcoming neurosurgical intervention and bleeding risk
Do not commit to glioma-directed surgical resection (vs. stereotactic biopsy) before considering CNS lymphoma — extensive resection of CNS lymphoma is not standard
key_reasoning_points: Imaging pattern of homogeneous enhancement, diffuse DWI restriction, periventricular and corpus-callosum involvement is atypical for GBM and characteristic of primary CNS lymphoma
Systemic features (weight loss, fevers, lymphadenopathy, oral thrush) plus high-risk sexual history mandate HIV testing in this presentation
Tissue diagnosis is essential before tumor-directed therapy; in suspected CNS lymphoma, deferring corticosteroids until biopsy when feasible preserves diagnostic yield

Mass effect with midline shift contraindicates lumbar puncture; CSF studies (cytology, flow cytometry, EBV PCR) — if eventually obtained — must wait until imaging-defined safety and ideally are paired with biopsy
Surgical resection is not the standard for primary CNS lymphoma; treatment is high-dose methotrexate-based chemotherapy ± whole-brain radiation

red_herrings.data_point: Outside-hospital preliminary diagnosis of 'brain tumor, likely GBM'
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the receiving team on glioma and toward empirical glioma management
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: MRI features (homogeneous enhancement, diffuse DWI restriction, periventricular/callosal involvement) plus systemic features (weight loss, lymphadenopathy, oral thrush) point to CNS lymphoma in an immunocompromised host; HIV testing and biopsy are mandatory before any tumor-directed therapy

metadata.diagnostic_challenge: Primary CNS lymphoma in an undiagnosed HIV/AIDS patient, initially referred as 'likely GBM.' Requires recognition of (1) clinical features of undiagnosed HIV, (2) imaging features distinguishing PCNSL from GBM (homogeneous vs ring enhancement, moderate vs high rCBV), and (3) fundamentally different management (chemotherapy, not surgery). Corticosteroids must be avoided before tissue diagnosis.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Off-pathway / atypical tumor histology (the case body diagnosis is not standard IDH-wildtype GBM); 4 required tools, 1 red herring(s); diagnosis requires recognizing mimic imaging patterns and adjusting management accordingly
case_body_concerns: Case body diagnosis is primary CNS lymphoma in HIV/AIDS but the case is filed under the GLIO-HG (high-grade glioma) condition prefix. Consider moving to a CNS lymphoma or HIV-CNS pack, or re-labeling as a glioma-mimic acceptance case (the GT preserved here describes the correct, non-glioma diagnosis from the case body).
